subject: Question on modeling richness in a two-step analysis

messages.author: 164105118b0b3573
messages.subject: Question on modeling richness in a two-step analysis
parts:
Dear all,

 We are interested in exploring the effects of some covariates on a bird community using hierarchical community models with DA, with covariates. In addition, we want to explore how species richness is affected by some covariates. We suspect some covariates affecting occupancy could also affect species richness.

 I was looking at section 11.6.4 in AHM book (Modeling species richness in a two-step analysis) and I wonder if it would be right using this kind of model. The example in the book for this analysis uses posteriors from occupancy model 5 which does not include covariates. So the question is, it is right to use the same covariates in the occupancy model (first step) to model richness (second step)?, or the 2 step approach only works when occupancy is not affected by any covariates (or only different ones as in richness)?

 My guess is that it would not be correct to use the same covariates used to model occupancy to model richness, then in that case can only make inferences on richness computed from the occupancy models (discarding the use of two step analysis).

 Thoughts?

 Thank you!

 Andrea

 PS: Is there any new references using this approach?

 

-----

Andrea Paula Goijman, Ph.D

Grupo Ecología, Biodiversidad y Gestión Ambiental en Agroecosistemas Instituto de Recursos Biológicos CIRN - INTA Castelar, Argentina 

Nicolas Repetto y de los Reseros s/n 1686 Hurlingham,

messages.author: 00ebeb6e0521112d
messages.subject: RE: Question on modeling richness in a two-step analysis
parts:
Dear Andrea,

I share your concerns about using the same covariates twice in such a two-step analysis. I think the best would be run two analyses, one for identifying covariates on occupancy and the other without covariates to get estimates of N for use in 2nd-stage modeling as in our book.

However, the very best would probably be to use a reparameterization of the community model due to Chris Sutherland and S. Tenan (see their 2-3 papers in MEE (I believe) recently) who develop a variant of the model where species richness IS a parameter and so can directly be modelled.

Best wishes  --  Marc

messages.subject: RE: Question on modeling richness in a two-step analysis
parts:
Hi Andrea,

 

Indeed this was the motivation of our (w/Simone Tenan) recent extensions of the community model:

 

1.       A multi-region community model for inference about geographic variation in species richness

2.       Quantifying spatial variation in the size and structure of ecologically stratified communities

 

We developed both using an application to an avian community.

Hopefully this is of use – which is the point ;) Please let me or Simone know if you have any questions!

 

Chris & Simone
